knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 4.2.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly lists exponential-family GLM response distributions and identifies the Normal special case?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: GLM responses sit in named exponential families. Package name or presence of exp() does not make a GLM. Normal is one family member, not the universal definition.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Binomial, Poisson, exponential, gamma, Normal. Normal is the special case, not the GLM definition.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating GLM as renamed OLS or requiring only Normal responses.

choices.label: Binomial, Poisson, exponential, gamma, and Normal are named exponential-family GLM responses. Normal with identity link is a special case inside the family list, not the definition of every GLM.
GLM is ordinary linear regression with a different software package name; no response distribution family is required.
Only Normal responses belong in a GLM; Poisson and binomial models are separate non-GLM procedures.
Any continuous response is automatically in the exponential family because the density can be written with an exp() somewhere.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 4.2.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Name three of binomial, Poisson, exponential, gamma, Normal as GLM responses. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Warrant family membership; refuse package-name GLM.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Family membership needs the exponential-family form tied to the response structure, not software branding or exp() alone.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Poisson, binomial, Normal with one-line warrants. Refuse package-name GLM.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Accepting package-name GLM or Normal-only family membership.

choices.label: Example: Poisson (counts with E[Y]=Var[Y]=μ); binomial (bounded proportion or count responses); Normal (continuous responses with constant variance). Each has an exponential-family density usable as a GLM response. Package name is not GLM; a GLM response sits in an exponential family with later eta and link.
GLM is just ordinary linear regression with a different software package name; family membership is marketing.
Only Normal belongs in the exponential family for GLM; Poisson and binomial are non-GLM legacy procedures.
Poisson belongs because the pmf contains exp(); that single algebraic feature is the family definition without mean-variance structure.

worked_example.title: Poisson natural parameter from claim frequency
worked_example.problem_statement: Weekly claim counts on a small commercial book are modelled as Poisson(λ). For λ = 4, write the pmf in exponential-family form exp{yθ − b(θ)} / a(φ) × c(y, φ) (with φ = 1), identify the natural parameter θ, and evaluate θ numerically. Also state why the Normal distribution is a special case within the same GLM exponential family, not a rival outside it.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Rewrite the Poisson pmf as exp{y ln λ − λ − ln y!} and read off θ = ln λ.

steps.label: Exponential-family rewrite
steps.attempt_cue: Take the log of the Poisson pmf and regroup the y-dependent term.
steps.explanation: Members of the exponential family admit a linear natural parameter multiplying y. For Poisson, that term is y ln λ.
steps.calculation: f(y) = exp{y ln λ − λ − ln(y!)};  θ = ln λ,  b(θ) = e^θ (= λ)

steps.label: Numeric natural parameter at λ = 4
steps.explanation: Substituting the given mean frequency produces a concrete natural parameter.

steps.label: Normal as a special case
steps.attempt_cue: State where Normal sits relative to Binomial, Poisson, exponential, and gamma.
steps.explanation: Binomial, Poisson, exponential, gamma, and Normal are all exponential-family GLM responses. Normal is the continuous identity-link special case, not an exclusion from the family.
steps.result: Normal is inside the family, not outside it

worked_example.final_answer: θ = ln λ = ln 4 ≈ 1.3863; Poisson is exponential-family with b(θ) = e^θ. Normal is a member of the same family, not a rival outside it.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Reporting θ = λ = 4 (the mean) instead of the natural parameter ln λ, or claiming Normal is excluded from the GLM exponential family.
